# Gravitational Evidence Geometry

This repository freezes one aggregate-only gravitational evidence row for a
model-free OpenWiki Claims demonstration. The source record is
`evidence/gravitational-evidence.json`.

The checked-in material does not include the simulation code, complete run
outputs, or the preimage identified by `source_artifact_sha256`. It can prove
whether the documented claims still match this checked-in JSON; it cannot by
itself reproduce the simulation or establish that the physical results are
correct.

The safe interpretation is deliberately narrow: compare the measured arms at
the same physical horizon, keep energy and trajectory outcomes separate, and
retain the stated single-initial-condition and cost limitations.

# Physical-Horizon Control Reconciliation

The evidence row retains the prior wording and the replacement facts together.
That makes the correction inspectable without presenting the superseded
sentence as current knowledge.

## Exact claim pair

### Superseded wording

> A smaller-timestep uncorrected trajectory control was not measured at this
> 10,000,000-step horizon and remains required for trajectory decisions.

Status: historical wording preserved inside the source disclosure. It is not
the current operating claim.

### Current physical-horizon claim

> The smaller-timestep uncorrected trajectory control was measured at the same
> 864,000,000,000-second physical horizon as `bare_dt_over_sqrtI`; it used
> 350,000,000 steps at 2,468.5714285714284 seconds per step.

Status: current claim grounded in the structured `matched_compute_control`
record and the principal row's horizon.

## Measured geometry

| Axis | Corrected arm | Smaller-timestep uncorrected control |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Physical horizon | 864,000,000,000 s | 864,000,000,000 s |
| Timestep | 86,400 s | 2,468.5714285714284 s |
| Steps | 10,000,000 | 350,000,000 |
| Maximum position RMS | 826.7024575894835 km | 766.8419412575681 km |
| Relative energy error | 3.110626167743352e-14 | 1.0174934063619424e-10 |
| Wall time | 314.00056314468384 s | 120.41298770904541 s |

The control was better on maximum position RMS and wall time, while the
corrected arm was substantially better on relative energy error. The source
therefore supports an energy-invariant result, not a general statement that the
corrected arm was better on every axis.

## Honest limitations

- The row contains one real-ephemeris initial condition.
- Energy improved while trajectory, angular momentum, and linear momentum did
  not improve.
- The released engine row is not an API-surface equivalence claim.
- The corrected arm used the highest-cost setting in the sweep. Its stated
  73.3-times wall-time cost against the principal uncorrected arm is not
  amortized in the energy figure.
- The checked-in file is a sanitized aggregate record. The simulation code,
  complete outputs, and the preimage named by `source_artifact_sha256` are
  absent, so this bundle proves claim-to-file freshness rather than the
  correctness of the underlying physics.
- The source explicitly limits the claim scope to energy-invariant
  conservation only.

# Gravitational Evidence Geometry

This repository contains one aggregate-only gravitational evidence row under
`evidence/gravitational-evidence.json`. The row uses the
`ektorus.paired-evidence.v1` schema at revision `2026-08-20.1` and labels
itself as sanitized aggregate data.

The recorded system is a real-ephemeris, three-body case using the WHFast
integrator. Its principal row uses 10,000,000 steps at 86,400 seconds per step,
which gives a physical horizon of 864,000,000,000 seconds.

## Reading contract

- Compare the corrected arm and the smaller-timestep control at the same
  physical horizon, not at the same step count.
- Keep energy conservation separate from trajectory, angular-momentum, and
  linear-momentum outcomes.
- Treat the old “control was not measured” sentence as preserved superseded
  wording, not as the current operating claim.
- Preserve the single-initial-condition, API-equivalence, and compute-cost
  limitations.

See [Physical-Horizon Control Reconciliation](geometry/physical-horizon-control.md)
for the exact old/current claim pair and the measured tradeoff.

## Trust boundary

The generated Claims can show whether this wiki still matches the checked-in
JSON. This repository does not contain enough material to reproduce the
simulation or independently establish the physical result.
